A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same simulator framework and research work. Their text, tables, figures, and Appendices A–H are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: V3 reports original dialogue simulations, agent fine-tuning experiments, error analyses, and human evaluations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains original simulation, fine-tuning, error-analysis, and human-evaluation results, including the benchmark results in Tables 1–4 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The collaborative simulator, state tracker, ending verifier, and four non-collaborative modules are unchanged. Appendix F's benchmark adaptations and Appendix G's prompts already appear in v3.

E1.justification: Both versions cover MultiWOZ, τ-bench, ColBench, and MINT's HotpotQA, HumanEval, TheoremQA, and GSM8K tasks. V4's prominent extension results already appear in v3's Appendix F; single- and combined-behavior simulations remain.

E2.justification: PBUS remains the simulator baseline, and the corresponding retained agent experiments use the same model sets. V4's main-text ColBench/MINT table repeats the existing three-model comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix E drops the six-pair combined-behavior protocol and its separate realism/coherence questions, retaining the single-behavior protocol. V4 still mentions both studies, so the reported design becomes incomplete without establishing that experiments were rerun. Benchmark settings and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 removes the empirical analysis of realism and coherence under combined behaviors presented in v3's Figure 5a. Step-limit sensitivity, goal-alignment validation, error analyses, training-mixture comparisons, and dialogue case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: V4 removes Appendix E's explicit sampling seed of 42 and makes four-trial averaging explicit for ColBench/MINT in Table 2. These are reporting changes; neither increased runs nor new uncertainty-estimation procedures are established.

E6.justification: V4 corrects Qwen3-235b-a22b's unavailable-service relative SR in the prose from 30.2% to 80.2%, matching unchanged Table 1. It removes combined-mode human results, including 47.8% unavailable-service and 37.8% tangential win rates against PBUS. The overall human-evaluation summary changes from approximately 60% to 70%, although retained single-mode bars are identical. Matched benchmark and fine-tuning scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs. The behavioral definitions, goal-alignment descriptions, and mathematical content remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction broadens the implementation contribution from MultiWOZ/τ-bench to various settings, while dropping explicit assertions that current agent performance may be overestimated and that extension requires only API/task descriptions. The central four-behavior, goal-alignment, and agent-vulnerability claims remain.

C2.justification: V4 removes the explanation linking weak combined-mode human ratings to unnatural behavior pairings, although Appendix D.8 retains general co-occurrence caveats. The revised human-evaluation discussion instead explicitly attributes agent degradation to realistic challenging behaviors rather than unrealistic generation.

D1.justification: V3 promises code and datasets upon publication; v4 states that code is released and supplies a repository address. Existing prompts, preprocessing instructions, QLoRA hyperparameters, hardware, and training-data details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds criticism of prior simulators' reliance on LLM-as-a-judge and positions goal-alignment enforcement as mitigation. It also elaborates Mehri et al.'s judge-based reward. The cited-work set is unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 edits the abstract, introduction, related work, and results narrative; gives fine-tuning its own Section 4.3; and promotes existing Appendix D.7/F.2 discussion into the main text. Human-evaluation prose is shortened, and publication, affiliation, and acknowledgement text is updated. Most document structure and prose remain.

P2.justification: V4 combines existing ColBench/HotpotQA results into main-text Table 2 and moves former Table 20 to Table 3. Figures 4 and 5 are placed together, Figure 5 loses its combined-mode panel, and appendix example tables and Figure 7 labels are enlarged. Most displays retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: V4 improves readability, corrects numerical and cross-reference errors, and supplies code-access information. However, removing the combined-behavior human results and detailed protocol weakens evidence for realistic combined simulation, while Section 4.4 and Appendix E still claim both studies. The unchanged single-behavior plot does not establish an improved win rate. This loss of evidential completeness outweighs the limited presentation and access-information gains.
